[[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] (2012–2014) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Consensus second team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2014 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2014]]) * 2× First team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] (2013–2014) * MVC Newcomer of the Year (2013) * NCAA All-Final Four team ([[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013]]) * 2× [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] Division III Player of the Year (2011–2012) * 2× [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] All-American (2011–2012) }} '''Cleanthony Early''' (born April 17, 1991) is an American [[basketball]] player. He was an All-American college player at [[Wichita State University]]. A 6'8" [[Forward (basketball)|forward]], Early was a [[junior college]] star at [[Sullivan County Community College]], where he was the two-time Division III [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] Player of the Year. After considering offers from major conference schools, he signed with [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] and coach [[Gregg Marshall]].{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Hurricane Irene helped Wichita State recruit Cleanthony Early | work = [[The Herald (Everett)|The Herald]] | date = April 6, 2013 | url = http://www.heraldnet.com/article/20130406/SPORTS/704069929 | accessdate = November 25, 2013}} Early made an immediate impact for the Shockers, averaging 13.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 5.4 [[rebounds per game]]. He was named first team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference]] and the MVC Newcomer of the Year.{{cite web | last = Suellentrop | first = Paul | title = Wichita State’s Cleanthony Early earns All-MVC honors | work = [[Wichita Eagle]] | date = October 30, 2013 | url = http://www.kansas.com/2013/03/05/2702695/wichita-states-cleanthony-early.html | accessdate = November 25, 2013}} In the post-season, Early led the team to the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013 Final Four]] in [[Atlanta]]. In the Shockers' semifinal game against eventual champion Louisville, Early scored 24 points and collected 10 rebounds in a narrow 72–68 loss.[http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330960097 Wichita State Shockers vs. Louisville Cardinals - Recap - April 06, 2013 - ESPN:] He was named to the All-Final Four team for his efforts.{{cite web | last = | first = | title = MBB: Early Named Final Four All-Tournament | work = [[Wichita State Shockers]] | date = April 9, 2013 | url = http://www.goshockers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=7500&ATCLID=207124060 | accessdate = November 25, 2013}} Going into his senior season, Early garnered widespread national attention. He was named preseason Player of the Year for the Missouri Valley Conference{{cite web | last = | first = | title = 2013-14 MVC Men's Basketball Preseason Team, Poll | work = [[Missouri Valley Conference]] | date = October 30, 2013 | url = http://www.mvc-sports.com/mbasketball/news/2013-14/6914/2013-14-mvc-mens-basketball-preseason-team-poll/ | accessdate = November 25, 2013}} and was named to the preseason top 50 watch lists for the [[John Wooden Award|John Wooden]]{{cite web | last = | first = | title = John R. Wooden Award Presented by Wendy's Reveals 2013-14 Preseason Top 50 | work = [[John Wooden Award]] | date = November 12, 2013 | url = http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1460 | accessdate = November 25, 2013}} and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]] Awards for national player of the year.{{cite web | last = | first = | title = 2013-2014 Men's 50-Player Watch List | work = [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]] | date = | url = http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1460 | accessdate = November 25, 2013}} Early helped lead the [[2013–14 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2013–14 team]] to an undefeated 34–0 record entering the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], becoming the first team in NCAA [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] men's basketball to do so [[1990–91 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|in over two decades]].{{cite news|url=http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/03/09/wichita-state-wins-mvc-ncaa-tournament-berth-fred-van-vleet/?eref=sihp |title=Wichita State reigns as MVC champions, finishes regular season at 34-0 |first=Michael |last=Beller |work=One and One |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |date=March 9, 2014 |accessdate=March 9, 2014}} Cleanthony put up an impressive effort in an attempt to help the Shockers advance to the sweet sixteen, with 31 points and 7 rebounds on 12/17 shooting. The Shockers ended up losing to Kentucky 78-76, ending their hopes of a final four repeat. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.goshockers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=7500&ATCLID=205717296 Wichita State bio] {{2014 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Persondata | NAME = Early, Cleanthony | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = Mr. Not Late | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = April 17, 1991 | PLACE OF BIRTH = | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Early, Cleanthony}} [[Category:1991 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2013 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York]] [[Category:Forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Junior college men's basketball players in the United States]] [[Category:Wichita State Shockers men's basketball players]]
